lines.text: An automatic press targets a U A diploma. One question stops it. Who earned this?
AI Engaged is a draft the Board discusses today.
It proposes six principles, four priorities from classrooms to Arctic research, and five expectations including literacy, security, and oversight.
But tools should deepen learning, not replace the effort that builds competence.
So a U A credential would certify what the student earned.
And one framework would not mean one classroom rule.
U A A, U A F, and U A S keep curriculum judgment. Faculty choose AI by course.
A coordinating council would share tools and training.
Then the diploma flips into a second trust test.
The draft addresses predictive AI affecting student progress or business operations.
Examples include admissions, financial aid, advising, and H R analytics.
Those uses would need documented evaluation and meaningful human oversight.
Strong words. But meaningful and earned are not measurements.
It defines neither, nor a reviewer's power.
So the plan must survive its own test.
A twelve-month clock waits behind glass.
It has not started. This framework has not been adopted.
If adopted, institutions get one year to build policies and plans.
Then Alaska gets evidence. Did AI deepen learning? Did oversight matter? Does the diploma still mean what it says?
The machine can help. A human pulls the press.
